tasks.title: The repository's front page is one word
tasks.goal: README.md contains only '# seraph' on a now-public repository, so the first thing a visitor reads says nothing while 20KB of real documentation sits in docs/USING.md they have to go and find.
tasks.description:
The repository went public today. Its front page says '# seraph'.

That is the emptiest possible statement on the front door of a project whose entire thesis is that a document must not say something the code does not do. docs/USING.md is 20KB of careful, verified writing; a visitor is given no reason to open it.

WHY IT IS WORTH THE NEXT TWENTY MINUTES. Every defect closed today shared one shape — a thing asserting more or less than was true: a hook file reported as installed when nothing read it, an entry in a table standing in for an observation, a board a clone was about to erase. A README claiming what the project does not yet do would be the same defect, in the one file nobody reviews because nobody expects prose to need checking.

WHAT IT MUST NOT DO. Claim enforcement for the five harnesses nobody has watched refuse a write. Promise the Index, the event log, or the get_board_summary filters. Describe a day of real work that has not happened. The honest version is shorter and more useful than the impressive one, and this board has already spent a day insisting so.
tasks.acceptance:
1. README.md states what seraph is, what it does and what it deliberately does not, in the project's own plain voice — accurate against the code, not aspirational. [ ]
2. It carries a getting-started a reader can copy and run. [ ]
3. Every claim about harness enforcement matches what `seraph hook` reports: one verified refusal, the rest unverified, and the states spelled out. [ ]
4. It links to docs/USING.md rather than duplicating it, and says which file answers which question. [ ]
5. Nothing in it promises something from the roadmap, which is deferred by decision. [ ]
6. Done through the board with the claim held by the session that did the work. [ ]

tasks.title: Record Phase 4 two-harness verification
tasks.goal: ROADMAP.md Phase 4 is the thesis check and it is the only phase with no artifact. Record what actually happened when two independent harness sessions were run against this repository's real board, so the stop condition has evidence behind it rather than a checkbox.
tasks.description:
PHASE 4 RUN — 2026-10-02, repository seraph, real board (.seraph/state.db, WAL, schema v2), real work (TASK-101, roadmap scope sync). Claim TTL 30m (internal/board/lifecycle.go ClaimTTL). Run length about eleven minutes.

WHAT HAPPENED, IN ORDER

1. A — harness omp, session omp-20261002T103448Z-a2d49cc5. Prompted with no mention of Seraph, the board, or any tool; told only to read the repo's own agent instruction files first, as a real client would load them automatically. It read AGENTS.md, called claim_task on TASK-101, and set it in_progress. Board rendered: claimed by: omp (session omp-20261002T103448Z-a2d49cc5, until 2026-10-02T11:05:05Z).

2. B — harness omp, session omp-20261002T103928Z-b09e5d. Read the board, found TASK-101 in progress under a session it did not start, and attempted to claim it. Refused. Verbatim:

{"reason":"CLAIM_HELD_BY_ANOTHER_SESSION","message":"TASK-101 is claimed by another session until 2026-10-02T11:05:05Z; do not start this work","holder":{"harness":"omp","session":"omp-20261002T103448Z-a2d49cc5","expires":1790939105}}

3. B edited nothing and did not pursue the hold by another route. It reported the refusal as the correct answer. get_task confirmed the holder independently of the error payload.

4. A completed the ROADMAP.md edits and moved TASK-101 to done at 2026-10-02T10:42:11Z. The server cleared the claim on completion.

5. B re-read the board: TASK-101 in Done, claim null, updated 2026-10-02T10:42:11Z, the claimed-by line gone.

PHASE 4'S THREE QUESTIONS

- Do harnesses read the Rules, or ignore them? OBSERVED: yes, for one harness. A was given a prompt naming none of this and found the workflow through AGENTS.md. One harness, one run — not a survey.
- Does anyone read KANBAN.md, or only call tools? NOT OBSERVED. Every participant drove the board through tools. B compared its tool read against .seraph/KANBAN.md as a consistency check and they agreed, but nobody used the file as a source of truth.
- Is claiming before work a feature or a tax? NOT OBSERVED. A claimed once without comment; B treated the refusal as correct without pushing back. An uncontended eleven-minute run cannot distinguish a feature from a tax.

STOP CONDITION VERDICT: UNRESOLVED. Not a pass.

The mechanical half passed end to end on real data: claim, refusal with a named holder, completion, and propagation to a second reader all behaved as specified. The thesis half was not exercised. Both sessions were the same harness product, the run was minutes rather than the day the phase asks for, no session was ever contended, and two of the three questions produced no evidence. The seventh Definition-of-done box — "Two different harnesses coordinate on one task in one repository" — should be read as unchecked until a second harness product is in the loop; a session of the same client is not a different harness.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT: a full day of real work with at least one participant that is not omp. doctor already reports Claude Code and opencode as present but unregistered, so neither needs installing first. Wiring the gate would make the check stronger than social convention, since an unclaimed write would then be actually refused rather than merely discouraged.

INCIDENTAL FINDINGS

- TASK-101 was reopened once during verification, because its first pass left the Phase 0 line implying main.go dispatches only serve/install/doctor. The board caught an incomplete pass; it did not rubber-stamp it.
- The repository contains zero *_test.go files, so every phase check in ROADMAP.md is manual and CLI-driven. This run's evidence is the same kind as the six checked boxes: a transcript, not a suite.
- One tooling error was surfaced and recovered mid-run: passing a status where a triage label belongs returns INVALID_TRIAGE naming the allowed set. That is the error taxonomy working as designed.

The verdict and its limits are also written into ROADMAP.md Phase 4, where someone deciding whether to push on will actually read them.

This task gets a second harness product genuinely into the loop on this repository, so the box is either earned or refuted by evidence rather than left unchecked.
tasks.description:
SECOND ATTEMPT 2026-10-02, via opencode. Claude Code is out of scope by the owner's decision — not installed, no credentials to be had.

MODEL CHANGE (done, as asked). ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json `model`: opencode/minimax-m2.1 → opencode/big-pickle. Backed up first at /tmp/opencode-config-backup-20261002T182055Z/home/dimasajiwardhana/.config/opencode/opencode.json. Rewritten through jq into the existing inode, so mode 664 and owner dimasajiwardhana are unchanged and all six top-level keys survive. `orchestrator`, the default_agent, carries no model override, so it inherits the new value — confirmed in the TUI header: 'Orchestrator · Big Pickle · OpenCode Zen'. The other six agents keep their github-copilot models, untouched.

RESULT: the model change does not unblock opencode.

- `opencode run` → 'Error: OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode'
- opencode TUI in a pty, same model → the same error, rendered inside the session view. So it is not a headless restriction.
- `opencode run -m opencode/deepseek-v4-pro` → 'Error: Upstream request failed: Insufficient account funds'
- `opencode run -m github-copilot/gpt-5-mini` → 'Error: Forbidden: unauthorized: not licensed to use Copilot'
- `opencode run -m openrouter/z-ai/glm-4.5-air` → 'Error: Missing Authentication header'
- ollama → not installed, so no local-model route

Every remaining path is closed by the account, not by the configuration: no OpenCode Zen subscription, no Copilot licence, no openrouter key, no funds. Nothing further can be done from here.

ALSO: `opencode mcp list` reports 'No MCP servers configured'. Seraph is not registered with opencode, so even a working model would have needed `opencode mcp add` first. Worth knowing that opencode and the board had no connection at all before this attempt.

STILL TRUE FROM THE FIRST ATTEMPT: opencode is 'cannot enforce' in `seraph hook` — its tool.execute.before hook cannot block, so it could coordinate on the board but never host an enforced gate. It was always the weaker of the two candidates.

TO UNBLOCK, someone has to authenticate a harness. The cheapest is Claude Code (`claude` → /login): it is the only candidate whose hook surface can actually block, so it is the only one that would strengthen the gate half as well as the coordination half. Once logged in this is one `claude -p` invocation with --mcp-config and --strict-mcp-config, which writes nothing to ~/.claude.json.

tasks.title: Act on the three-audit review of this session's work
tasks.goal: Three independent reviewers audited the work recorded as done today. Every finding is a case of a document or a board annotation claiming something the code does not do — the exact defect class this project exists to end, committed by this session. Fix the false statements and the one overstated detection claim.
tasks.description:
Acted on findings from AuditCode, AuditDocs and AuditBoard.

One methodological correction worth recording, because it nearly produced a wrong fix. My first attempt at verifying the no-session branch used a hand-copied state.db and reported 'allow' where the document says 'deny', which would have led me to weaken a correct sentence. The copy was the problem, not the doc: copying a WAL-mode database without its -wal file yields a board the gate reads as holding no claims, which takes the 'another session holds a claim; this hook cannot tell which' path. Re-run on the real board the gate denies, exactly as documented. Lesson recorded rather than buried: test the gate against a database seraph itself created, never a hand-copied one.

Also corrected in this pass: my own TASK-105 description, which had repeated the two false gate claims verbatim. Fixing the document while leaving the same falsehood on the board would have been the defect class wearing a different hat.

tasks.title: Four packages and three documents exist only on disk
tasks.goal: git reports internal/gate, internal/dashboard, internal/tui and internal/webui as untracked in full, along with docs/USING.md, DESIGN.md and PRODUCT.md, so a fresh checkout of this repository contains neither the claim gate, nor the human-facing surfaces, nor the documentation that describes them.
tasks.description:
Found while closing TASK-109, whose FINDING 2 named only internal/installer/hooks.go. Checking git status properly showed the finding was much larger.

git status --short, untracked entries only:

    ?? .claude/  ?? .cursor/  ?? .kiro/  ?? .omp/
    ?? .impeccable/
    ?? .seraph/KANBAN.md  ?? .seraph/board.json
    ?? DESIGN.md  ?? PRODUCT.md  ?? docs/USING.md
    ?? internal/dashboard/  ?? internal/gate/  ?? internal/tui/  ?? internal/webui/

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE ORIGINAL FINDING. internal/installer/hooks.go was one file whose fix could be lost. internal/gate is the entire claim gate — command.go and gate.go — and it is untracked, so a clone of this repository has no gate at all. ROADMAP.md carries a Carried-forward section naming gate, tui, webui and dashboard as shipping in this tree, and docs/USING.md documents the gate's four behaviours in detail. None of that survives a checkout. That is the same defect class TASK-109 exists to close, one directory up and considerably larger.

WHAT WAS DONE IN TASK-109, AND WHY NOT HERE. TASK-109's criterion 4 forbids touching another path's git state, so only internal/installer/hooks.go was staged there. Staging four packages and three documents is the owner's decision, not a side effect of a cleanup: it changes what a clone contains, and criterion 5 here keeps that explicit.

NOT VERIFIED, AND WORTH CHECKING BEFORE ANYONE ACTS. Whether .seraph/.gitignore already covers the two snapshots depends on its contents, which this task has not audited. Whether .claude/, .cursor/, .kiro/ and .omp/ are wanted in the repository is a judgement about generated harness configuration, not a defect, and belongs to the owner.
tasks.acceptance:
1. Every package under internal/ and every document the roadmap or USING.md references is either tracked or deliberately ignored, with the reason written down. [MET. 55 files tracked after the merge — all twelve packages, all four ADRs, USING.md, DESIGN.md, PRODUCT.md, prd.md, both board snapshots. Every ignore rule resolves to a named line with a reason beside it, and nothing is left untracked.]
2. A clean clone of this repository builds and passes go vet — verified on the clone, not on this working tree. [MET, on the clone and not the tree: git clone into a fresh temp directory carried 55 files; go build ./... clean, go vet ./... clean, go test ./... green at 19 tests across three packages. The working tree was not consulted for any of it.]
3. seraph install, doctor and hook behave the same on that clean clone. [MET, all three run in the clone. `install --dry-run` reported Codex, Copilot CLI and Gemini CLI unchanged, Claude Code, Cursor and omp 'would install' — correct, since those are project-scoped and gitignored — and Kiro, Zed, opencode advisory only. `hook` read project targets 'not installed' and user-scope targets 'installed, unverified', which is the correct reading of a clone that has never been installed into. `doctor` resolved the repository, created state.db, reported schema v2 and exited 0. The clone was left clean by all three.]
4. The generated harness hook directories and the .seraph snapshots are each either committed deliberately or ignored, and the choice is recorded. [MET. Snapshots committed, following the intent already stated in .seraph/.gitignore. The five hook paths ignored, each with the absolute-path reason written beside it, alongside GitHub's Go template entries under a '── Seraph ──' section.]
5. No commit is created without the owner's explicit say-so. [MET. The owner gave it explicitly in conversation, twice, naming commit and push. Two commits: 8e7207a 'Initial commit: seraph v1' and dc2a5f8 merging the remote's initial branch. Both pushed; main and master both point at dc2a5f8. A credential scan over every staged path ran first and found nothing.]

THE FIRST CLONE RETURNED TWO FILES, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. The repository had been created on GitHub with a default branch `main` holding a placeholder README and the standard Go .gitignore. The work went to `master`. A clone takes the remote's default, so the verification in criterion 2 came back with two files and no go.mod — the exact failure the criterion exists to catch, caught on its first run. Merged `origin/main` into `master` with --allow-unrelated-histories, resolved the add/add conflict on .gitignore by keeping GitHub's Go template and appending the project-specific rules beneath it, then fast-forwarded `main` to the merge. Both branches now carry the code, and the README was preserved rather than overwritten.

AND THE CLONE CHECK FOUND A REAL DEFECT, RECORDED AS TASK-116. On that clone `seraph doctor` prints `tasks 0` and then `KANBAN.md … DIFFERS from the board — any tool call rewrites it`, twice. state.db is gitignored as machine-local and always was right to be; the two snapshots beside it are committed and meant to be read. So a clone arrives with the whole history in two files and no database, and the first seraph tool call on it overwrites that history with an empty board. Until today there was no clone to get wrong. There is one now, and it is the first thing anyone will do.

tasks.title: One session identity, so a claim and a gate stop disagreeing
tasks.goal: claim_task accepts any session_id a caller types while the gate reads SERAPH_SESSION_ID, so a session that claims under one id is refused by the gate as though it held nothing, with a message it cannot tell apart from an empty board.
tasks.description:
Found live during the Phase 4 run of 2026-10-05 and recorded by harness B in TASK-109's description, where it has an acceptance criterion but no criterion of its own.

THE DEFECT, AS OBSERVED. internal/gate/gate.go:169-175 — the switch inside liveClaims has three cases: sess == "" or expired, so unclaimed; sess == session, so held. A task held by a DIFFERENT live session matches none of them, so it lands in neither list. That is arguably right for claimability, and it is what makes the message wrong: the caller is told only that it holds no task and how many tasks are unclaimed. A session whose claim exists under another identity is told the same thing as a session on an empty board. Harness B hit exactly this: it claimed under its omp UUID, the gate read SERAPH_SESSION_ID, and the refusal read like a policy decision rather than an identity mismatch.

THE RELATED GAP. internal/gate/command.go:53 resolves the session from the payload alone. The omp hook passes process.env.SERAPH_SESSION_ID, so a hook caller and an MCP caller in the same session can legitimately hold different strings. One environment variable, read in two places by two different subsystems, is the whole of the disagreement.

WHY criterion 3 IS A WARNING AND NOT A REFUSAL. Harnesses genuinely differ in what they can pass. omp has SERAPH_SESSION_ID; a harness without it has only whatever it types. Refusing on mismatch would lock out every caller that cannot supply the ambient value, which is the deadlock this project already hit once with create_task. The honest amount is to say so.

WHY TESTS COME WITH THIS ONE. The repository has zero *_test.go files — recorded as an incidental finding in TASK-102 — so every check in ROADMAP.md is manual. This change alters a decision contract, which is exactly the case worth a regression net, and the test is part of the change rather than a follow-up.

The last item in the plan at /tmp/seraph-defect-plan.md. TASK-110 fixed Kiro, which was the first PROVEN instance; this is the class.

TASK-108 recorded payloads fed directly to `seraph gate` — Read 0, Bash 2, holder 0 and the rest — and annotated the result as the gate's four behaviours being verified. tasks.title: The omp gate is written to a directory omp never reads
tasks.goal: seraph install writes the claim gate to .omp/hooks/pre/ and ~/.omp/hooks/pre/, and shapes it as an ExtensionFactory, but omp discovers hooks only in ~/.omp/agent/hooks/, .claude/hooks/pre/ and ~/.codex/hooks, and takes HookAPI — so the gate never loaded and no omp write has ever been gated.
tasks.description:
The open question TASK-110's scope note left: the omp gate was installed, reported installed, and did not fire in the session that installed it. Answered here, from omp's own shipped package rather than from inference.

WHAT omp DISCOVERS. Its bundle contains exactly three discovery strings: 'Load hooks from .claude/hooks/pre/ and .claude/hooks/post/', 'Load hooks from ~/.codex/hooks and .codex/hooks/', and 'Load hooks from Claude Code marketplace plugins'. Its own examples/hooks/README.md adds the native location: 'cp permission-gate.ts ~/.omp/agent/hooks/'. There is no .omp/hooks/ discovery path anywhere in the package.

WHAT seraph WRITES. The omp target is Project: true with Path '.omp/hooks/pre/seraph-gate.ts', and an earlier run also left ~/.omp/hooks/pre/seraph-gate.ts. Neither directory is read by omp. The file was inert from the moment it was written.

THE SECOND MISMATCH. The generated module type-imports ExtensionFactory, which lives in dist/types/extensibility/extensions/types.d.ts — the EXTENSIONS subsystem. Hooks take HookAPI, from dist/types/extensibility/hooks/types.d.ts. Both types ship; seraph imported the wrong one. That alone would break the module even in a directory omp does read.

PROOF BEFORE FIX. A probe module written to ~/.omp/agent/hooks/ using HookAPI and the plain default-export shape was run against a real omp subprocess holding no claim. The shell command was refused with the gate's own message and /tmp/omp-gate-probe.txt was confirmed absent. The mechanism works; only the generator was wrong.

tasks.title: A verified entry that cannot go stale silently
tasks.goal: The `verified` registry records a harness build that somebody watched refuse a write, but nothing compares that build against the harness actually installed, so an upgrade silently keeps claiming coverage nobody re-earned.
tasks.description:
TASK-114 ended with omp 18.0.3 in the registry and one witnessed refusal behind it. That entry is true today and decays tomorrow: upgrade omp, and `seraph hook` keeps printing 'enforcing (verified omp 18.0.3)' for a build nobody watched refuse anything.

This is the same shape as the two defects just fixed. A file on disk read as enforcement; an entry in a table read as enforcement. Both were a static fact standing in for an observed one. The difference is that this one is at least self-aware — it names the build it applies to. It just never checks whether that build is still installed.

WHY NOT AN AUTOMATED PROBE. TASK-113 decided against one because kiro cannot run tools headlessly, so a probe would skip the harnesses most worth checking. That reasoning still holds for kiro, and it now does not hold for omp: TASK-114 proved an omp subprocess can be driven and refused. So a probe is possible for one harness — but it costs a model call per verification, needs a live board to be meaningful, and would prove enforcement only at the moment it ran rather than for the build recorded. Comparing versions is deterministic, free, offline, and catches precisely the decay that matters: a silent upgrade.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not re-earn an entry. A build that matches still has only the one refusal behind it, and re-watching one is a person's job with a real harness in front of them.

[MET: VerifyRecorded only reads; nothing writes to verified, and no harness is spawned beyond its own --version. 3. A passing --verify on omp 18.0.3 says the entry holds; the comparison is a pure function with tests over the string forms real binaries emit. [MET: versionHolds is a pure function with five cases in internal/installer/hooks_test.go: the exact 'omp/18.0.3' against a recorded '18.0.3', a version with a trailing description, a genuinely upgraded build, a harness that reported nothing, and an entry carrying no token. The last two matter most — an empty token must never read as holding, or every entry would pass vacuously.]

The function checks that the recorded token appears in what the binary reports, and the tests pin both directions.

A STALE COMMENT CORRECTED ALONG THE WAY. The doc comment on `verified` still opened 'verified is empty, and that is the honest state rather than an omission' — written when TASK-113 landed it, false the moment TASK-114 added an entry. It now describes what the registry is for and names both inert-gate incidents it exists to distinguish.

WHAT THIS STILL DOES NOT DO. It does not re-earn an entry, and 'holds' says exactly that. omp 18.0.3 still has one witnessed refusal behind it and nothing more; a matching version means the claim has not expired, not that it has been reconfirmed. The other ten harnesses remain 'installed, unverified', and --verify says nothing about them because there is nothing recorded to check.

tasks.title: A fresh clone's first tool call erases the board it shipped with
tasks.goal: state.db is deliberately gitignored as machine-local, but KANBAN.md and board.json are committed, so a fresh clone has an empty database beside a full set of snapshots and `seraph doctor` reports the committed board as differing — meaning the first tool call on a fresh clone overwrites the project's entire task history with an empty board.
tasks.description:
Found by doing what TASK-111 criterion 2 asked: cloning this repository fresh and running the three commands on the clone instead of on the working tree.

WHAT HAPPENS. The clone is correct in every way that was checked — 55 files, go build, go vet, 19 tests green, and install/doctor/hook all behaving as designed. But `seraph doctor` on the clone prints:

    tasks 0
    KANBAN.md 64059 bytes, 4m30s ago, DIFFERS from the board — any tool call rewrites it
    board.json 65721 bytes, 4m30s ago, DIFFERS from the board — any tool call rewrites it

WHY. .seraph/.gitignore excludes state.db as machine-local, and that has always been right — a database is not a document. The two rendered snapshots beside it are committed, deliberately, because they are meant to be read. So a clone arrives holding the whole history in two files and no database at all, and the first thing seraph writes is an empty board over the top of it.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW THAN IT DID. Until today the repository had no clone to get wrong. It has one, and it is the first thing anyone — including a future session of this one — will do.

WHAT WAS NOT DECIDED HERE. This is recorded, not fixed. The choice between refusing, seeding and documenting is a real product decision with a real cost to each, and it is not mine to make silently.
tasks.acceptance:
1. Reproduced on a clean clone with the literal output of `seraph doctor` and of the first mutating tool call. [MET. A simulated fresh clone of the changed tree — 57 tracked files, no .seraph/state.db — printed before the fix: 'tasks 0', 'KANBAN.md … DIFFERS from the board — any tool call rewrites it', twice. After: 'board restored 16 task(s) from the committed board.json', 'tasks 16', and both snapshots read 'current'.]
2. Decided, and the other two recorded as rejected. [CHOSEN by the owner: seed the database from the committed snapshot. REJECTED — refusing the first write: it protects the snapshots but leaves every new clone needing a manual step before it can do anything, and the snapshot would still be inconsistent with an empty database. REJECTED — document that snapshots are history rather than state: cheapest, and it makes the committed snapshots decorative, which contradicts the stated intent in .seraph/.gitignore that they are meant to be read.]
3. Stated in docs/USING.md. [MET. A 'Cloning a repository that already has a board' paragraph sits directly under the commit table that says the database is No and the snapshots are Yes — the exact pairing that caused this — with the real output, the zero-tasks-only rule, and what happens on a snapshot this build cannot read.]
4. No existing behaviour changes silently. [MET. SeedFromSnapshot returns immediately if the board holds a single task, so a board with live claims is never reachable, let alone overwritten. Tested both ways: a second seed on a populated board restores 0 and leaves the count at 3 in a board that had 2 seeded plus 1 live. Claims are restored rather than dropped — a claim from a commit is almost always expired and the gate treats it as no claim, but discarding the record would silently un-hold a task somebody was working on.]
5. Done through the board with the claim held by the session that did the work. [MET: claimed and marked done by session omp-20261005T030418Z-01a10a04. gofmt -l clean, go vet ./... clean, go test ./... green at 24 tests. No commit yet — this work is staged, not pushed.]

THE DETAIL THAT WOULD HAVE COST THE FEATURE ITS PURPOSE. id_sequence is created at last=100. Seeding tasks TASK-101 through TASK-116 without advancing it would leave the next create_task allocating 101 and colliding with a task the snapshot already holds — and that failure reads as a corrupted board rather than as arithmetic. The seed advances the sequence to the highest id it restored, and a test pins it.

WHY A SNAPSHOT FROM A FUTURE VERSION MUST FAIL WHOLE. The schema constrains status and priority with CHECK lists. A snapshot carrying a status this build does not know would fail the insert and abort the whole transaction, leaving nothing behind — rather than half-applying and producing a board that looks seeded and is not. Tested: an invented status is refused and the board is left at zero tasks.

WHERE THE SEED RUNS. internal/board, because that package owns the snapshot's shape and does not import internal/db. Called from the three places that open a board: mcp.Serve and dashboard.Open return the error, doctor reports it. The split is deliberate — doctor exists to describe a board and the fix is the reader's, but a server handed an empty board it would then overwrite is the failure this task exists to prevent, so there it stops the line.
